criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the check stage has a baseline of base-commit failures but no mapping from a failing test's reported file paths to the paths the job changed, so a failure from a concurrent change is indistinguishable from the job's own.
criteria.evidence: The new CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]/### Fixed and the new D186 'Decision' bullet both state, nearly word for word: "the check stage has a baseline of base-commit failures but no mapping from a failing test's reported file paths to the paths the job changed, so a failure from a concurrent change is indistinguishable from the job's own". Both also say the verifier sees no output for a check Athena ran itself. I confirmed that claim in check_result_view (verify.rs:62-88): it fills output_tail only when `r.reused && !r.passed`. Both name the fix where the gap starts (failure_paths, failure_path_finding, judge_with_tree, verifier_check_views).

findings.summary: A changed file is not on the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs
findings.evidence: The only change is the import line: `judge` is replaced by `judge_with_tree`, which verification.rs needs. It adds no behavior, but it is outside the listed deliverables. Planned checks.rs was not changed, which leaves no criterion unshown.

findings.summary: The path link is a heuristic over a 200-line output tail and cannot by itself tell a concurrent-change failure from the job's own
findings.evidence: `failure_paths` splits the output into tokens and keeps tokens that match tracked files (exact match, or a suffix match when the token has a '/'). This is a sound way to avoid false positives because only tracked files count. But the finding only states facts, and the check still fails. A panic line cut from the 200-line tail gives no finding. CHANGELOG and D186 state these limits openly, and the reading asked for an informational finding, not an excuse, so this is fine for now.

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asks, and every criterion is met. In verify.rs, `failure_paths` reads a failing check's output, keeps only files tracked at the base or the candidate, and splits them into files the job changed, files it did not change, and ambiguous names. `failure_path_finding` turns that into one Minor Athena finding that also says how the failure got past the baseline. `judge_with_tree` adds those findings after everything the unchanged `judge` produced, so the verdict and its reasons do not change and no refusal rule is added. In run/verification.rs, `verifier_check_views` puts the same text into the verifier's brief. Before this change, the verifier saw no output at all for a check Athena ran itself. The CHANGELOG entry and the new D186 name the root cause in the criterion's words. I ran `cargo test --locked -p athena-core verify`, the `verify::tests::` subset (75 passed) and `cargo test --locked -p athena-core a_failing_check_citing` (2 passed). All the new tests pass. Athena's recorded fails-without runs show they do not compile on the reverted tree. fmt, clippy and test passed in the CI run recorded for this exact SHA. There are two minor findings, neither blocking. First, run/mod.rs changed but is not on the deliverables list; the change is one import line. Second, the path link is a heuristic that works on the stored output tail only, and the change documents that limit openly. Verdict: pass.
